facts.title: vLLM RFC #5557: Disaggregated Prefilling via KV Cache Transfer (communicator + KV database)
facts.event_hint: Foundational vLLM design RFC proposing two abstractions (communicator, KV database) to transfer KV cache between vLLM instances and store it for on-demand reuse.
facts.problem: There are growing use cases requiring KV cache to be moved between vLLM instances or stored for later reuse — specifically (a) disaggregated prefilling, where KV cache produced on prefilling instances must reach decoding instances, and (b) querying fixed large document sets (software manuals, internal docs) whose combined KV cache exceeds GPU + CPU memory and must be stored externally and paged into GPU on demand.
facts.mechanism: The RFC proposes two new abstractions composed as 'vllm <-> communicator <-> KV database'. The communicator transfers data from a source to a destination, where each endpoint can be either a KV block living inside a vLLM instance or an entry in the KV database. The KV database uses the hash generated by vLLM's automatic prefix caching as the key and the corresponding KV cache tensor as the value, making stored cache addressable and reusable across instances.

evidence.claim: Two concrete motivating use cases are given: disaggregated prefilling (prefill instances -> decode instances) and persistent long-document KV storage paged to GPU on demand.
The proposed design introduces a 'communicator' that moves data src->dst where either endpoint can be a vLLM KV block or a database entry.
The 'KV database' uses the automatic-prefix-caching hash as key and the KV cache tensor as value.

Open design questions are explicitly listed: leveraging NVLink for faster transfer, pipelining the transfer, preventing blocks from being swapped out mid-transfer, and whether/ how to compress KV cache during transfer and who performs compression.
evidence.source_locator: Description > Proposed Change, challenge questions bullets

evidence.claim: The RFC was opened for community feedback over 'several weeks' and CC'd core vLLM maintainers (simon-mo, youkaichao, zhuohan123, cadedaniel, ywang96, WoosukKwon, LiuXiaoxuanPKU).

facts.evaluation_context: Design RFC (issue #5557, opened 2024-06-14), not an implementation or measurement paper. Scope is the vLLM serving stack. No hardware, workload size, or latency numbers are given.
facts.limitations: Explicit: this is an RFC soliciting design feedback, not a specification or implementation — the abstractions are described at a conceptual level. Explicit: the four sub-problems (NVLink use, pipelining, swap-safety, compression) are posed as open questions, not answered here. Inferred: nothing in the issue addresses cross-region / WAN placement, consistency, or multi-tenant isolation; the framing is single-cluster instance-to-instance transfer.
facts.project_relevance: This is the originating design for what became vLLM's kv_transfer_config / connector framework (the same connectors documented by Ray Serve in the sibling source). It is directly relevant to KVCache cross-node transfer and disaggregated inference (TPN). The 'KV database keyed by prefix-caching hash' idea is the conceptual ancestor of cross-engine/cross-region KV sharing stores (LMCache, Mooncake), and the open compression/pipelining questions prefigure the briefing's 'compression / incremental transfer / prefetch' sub-topic. It does not, by itself, address WAN economics.
source_notes: Source is the original GitHub issue (vllm-project/vllm #5557) — the primary source for this RFC, so primary_source_resolved = true.
The retrieved chunk is the issue body only (comments / resolution not captured); the actual implemented connector semantics live in later PRs and the Ray Serve / LMCache docs.
